{{Short description|Russian mathematician (born 1941)}}
'''Alexandr Sergeevich Mishchenko''' ({{langx|ru|Александр Сергеевич Мищенко}}; born August 18, 1941, in [[Rostov-on-Don]]) is a Russian mathematician, specializing in [[differential geometry]] and [[topology]] and their applications to mathematical modeling in the [[bioscience]]s.

==Education and career==
After completing undergraduate study in 1965 in the [[MSU Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics|Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics]] of [[Moscow State University]], Mishchenko became a graduate student in the Department of Higher Geometry and Topology of the same Faculty and graduated there in 1968 with [[Candidate of Sciences]] degree (PhD). His PhD thesis K-теория на категории бесконечных комплексов<ref>[http://www.nlr.ru/e-case3/sc2.php/web_gak/lc/61327/4#pict Мищенко, 1968, Каталог РНБ (Catalog RNL, Russian National Library]</ref> ([[K-theory]] on the [[Category (mathematics)|category]] of infinite [[Simplicial complex|complexes]]) was supervised by [[Sergei Novikov (mathematician)|Sergei Novikov]].<ref name=MathGen>{{MathGenealogy|id=62890|name=Alexander S. Mishchenko}}</ref> In 1973 Mishchenko received his Russian [[Doctor of Sciences]] degree (habilitation) with thesis Гомотопические инварианты неодносвязных многообразий<ref>[http://www.nlr.ru/e-case3/sc2.php/web_gak/lc/61327/2#pict Мищенко, 1974, Каталог РНБ (Catalog RNL, Russian National Library)]</ref> (Homotopy invariants of non-simply connected varieties).<ref name=MathGen/>

Mishchenko is since 1979 a full professor in the Department of Higher Geometry and Topology, Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics, Moscow State University. He also works at the [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]]. His research deals with geometry and topology,<ref>[http://letopis.msu.ru/peoples/2394 Летопись Московского университета. Мищенко А. С. (Annals of Moscow University. Mishchenko A.S.)]</ref> application of algebraic and functional methods in the theory of smooth [[Algebraic variety|varieties]] with non-commutative geometry and topology, and applications of geometry and topology to mathematical modeling in ecology, molecular biology, bioinformatics. He has done some research on the history of mathematics, mathematical education, and the history of teaching mathematics.<ref name=laudation>A. A. Bolibrukh, A. A. Irmatov, M. I. Zelikin, O. B. Lupanov, V. M. Maynulov, E. F. Mishchenko, M. M. Postnikov, Yu. P. Solov'ev, E. V. Troitskii, [http://www.mathnet.ru/php/archive.phtml?wshow=paper&jrnid=rm&paperid=469&option_lang=eng “Aleksandr Sergeevich Mishchenko (on his 60th birthday)”], Uspekhi Mat. Nauk, 56:6(342) (2001), 167–170; Russian Math. Surveys, 56:6 (2001), 1187–1191</ref> He is the author or coauthor of over 100 research articles.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mishchenko, Alexandr Sergeevich|website=Math-Net.Ru|url=http://www.mathnet.ru/eng/person8599}}</ref>

In 1970, he was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Nice.<ref>{{cite book|author=Mishchenko, A. S.|chapter=Extraordinary homology theories: bordism and K-theory|title=Actes du Congrès international des mathématiciens, 1–10 Septembre 1970, Nice|volume=Tome 2|pages=113–119}}</ref> In 1971 he was awarded, jointly with [[Victor Buchstaber]], the  [[Moscow Mathematical Society]] Prize for research on the K-theory of infinite-dimensional CW-complexes. In 1996 Mischenko, jointly with [[Anatoly Fomenko]], was awarded the State Prize of the Russian Federation in the field of science and technology for a series of works involving investigation of invariants of smooth manifolds and Hamiltonian dynamical systems. In 2006 Mishchenko was awarded the title of Honored Professor of Moscow State University.<ref name=laudation/>
